posts.name: sandeepkumar sudhakar surkute
posts.cooked:
Yes, I also solved only one question and getting 43 as score, I have written it in separate post.

@sayan @AtulPS @Subendu Kindly Request instructors to please consider these cases for re-oppe. This OPPE score would snatch a chance of scoring S in the course. Still the “ synchro status " was not working properly, sometimes it gave results, and sometimes it was throwing errors.

Please consider this is sincere student request to maintain better academic performance on our part.

Regards,

Sandeep

posts.name: Rohit Rai
posts.cooked:
@sayan sir Thank you for your reply regarding my OPPE scores. I wanted to clarify my situation further
For Question 1, I had initially solved it, but later I removed my answer and submitted the final version as blank. Since my final submission did not contain the solution, I feel it should not be counted as solved.
For Question 5, I had attempted it and was close to solving it, but due to a minor error, it did not pass. My intention in removing the earlier answer was to prepare for a proper retry in OPPE 2.

And similar thing happened in question 4 where all test cases were good only issue in my code was it was not printing single digit number with a zero it was just printing that number.
Seeing both these questions as i was close to solving them i decided to remove question 1 solution and work more retry giving Re-OPPE.

posts.name: Rohit Rai
posts.cooked:
@sayan sir as i had removed solution to question but i was assessed for it as well.
can i be eligible to Re OPPE as in my last submission of Q1 did not had answers and also i want to give re OPPE. So am i eligible for Re OPPE?

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: That is not possible, we have taken the highest score for each question, since we had to re-evaluate all questions post the exam, if you get more than 40, we cannot allot a reOPPE.

posts.name: sandeepkumar sudhakar surkute
posts.cooked:
At the end, I have lost chance for re-oppe due to mis-information during the live session about latest evaluation being the final one instead of the maximum of all evaluations. With that information only I ran and later commented some code to fail the question which did not work as planned. I had deliberately planned to re-do the OPPE because I had another OPPE on next day and wanted to score 100 in the SC.

Also if the VM would have run satisfactorily, At least two more questions I could have completed successfully except maybe awk question scoring at least 80. The speed of VM seriously took away some time. The compensation was 30 minutes but the VM was slow after approx 10-15 minutes in to the exam. We did not feel the pinch because first two questions were relatively lighter to tackle. By the time we complained about VM in exam, we were half way through time of the exam.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
22f3002925:

I ran and later commented some code to fail the question which did not work as planned. I had deliberately planned to re-do the OPPE

I hope you are aware that deliberately failing the OPPE is not allowed and not encouraged. This is the exact reason why reOPPE questions are harder, to discourage such practices.

There have been hundreds of students who have scored \frac{100}{100} in first OPPE despite the technical issues with the extra 30 minutes provided, and many more have performed well without resorting to such tactics.

If you have solved a question, you get marks for said question.

posts.name: sandeepkumar sudhakar surkute
posts.cooked:
@sayan Sir, I also don’t like to postpone OPPE due to any tactics. In the same week, I had 2 project viva’s, and 2 OPEEs of PDSA and SC, i.e. SC in the evening 9-11 PM, and PDSA the next morning at 09:30 AM. And all this I was to complete as full time working professional.

Flexibility of this online programme was the key motivation for me to join the programme along with a full time job.

Also, I had requested support to postpone PDSA OPPE to 23 or 24 Aug, which was not done by them. Only then I had decided to re-do the SC-OPPE in the second slot only from the perspective of appearing with full revision, and no other intention than to continue the good grades in the programme specially in my favourite subject of SC.

I accept the results and would like to clarify that there were no ill-intended tactics other than just to purely space out different OPPEs/ Project Vivas, since it was not done by Support automatically despite there being slots for PDSA on 23 and 24.

I respect my instructors and their decisions, therefore I would not like them to think that there were some tactics in there. Hence, this clarification from my side about the schedule I was facing for the OPPE week.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
I can understand your situation, it becomes hectic trying to manage multiple subjects/OPPE/project vivas in the same week.

(SC OPPE was 7pm to 9:30pm though, not 9pm to 11pm).

Usually the OPPE slots are not moved around and are mentioned before the registration in the grading document so that students can choose non-conflicting subjects in a term during registration. However, it might not always be possible to avoid conflicts.

However, since we had to perform a re-grade of all solutions post the OPPE due to submission issue, it leaves us no choice but to take the max of the attempts, so that the latest rescore does not override someone’s previously successful attempt.

posts.name: sandeepkumar sudhakar surkute
posts.cooked:
@sayan

Thanks for understanding.

P.S. And yes, the time of SC OPPE is as corrected in your reply. I erroneously wrote 9-11pm in my post.
